learning_objective: The learner will examine a chart of monthly page views for three components and answer five questions about totals, trends, and what the counts do and do not show, with at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: chart **sim-id:** usage-analytics-reader
**Library:** Chart.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine a chart of monthly page views for three components and answer five questions about totals, trends, and what the counts do and do not show, with at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Usage Analytics, Reuse Tracking (defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner answers five questions about the chart. An answer is correct when it matches the Correct answer column in Content. Mastery is at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt. Hovering over bars and toggling a component are exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Page views show that students learned. (2) A drop in views means the resource got worse. (3) The most viewed component is the best one. **Instructional Rationale:** Examining a chart with a calendar effect is an Analyze-level action. A chart with a holiday dip and one dominant component teaches the learner to separate the pattern from its causes. **Content:** The data, shown as a grouped bar chart with months on the horizontal axis and page views on the vertical axis (made up, for the Watershed Basics components over six school months): | Month | Reading | Quiz | Simulation | Month total | |---|---|---|---|---| | September | 180 | 120 | 60 | 360 | | October | 420 | 300 | 210 | 930 | | November | 380 | 290 | 270 | 940 | | December | 150 | 100 | 90 | 340 | | January | 90 | 60 | 40 | 190 | | February | 310 | 240 | 190 | 740 | | Six-month total | 1,530 | 1,110 | 860 | 3,500 | The five questions: | # | Question | Choices | Correct answer | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Which component had the most page views over the six months? | Reading; Quiz; Simulation | Reading | It had 1,530 views. | | 2 | Which month had the highest total? | October; November; February | November | Its total is 940. | | 3 | What most likely explains the low December and January totals? | The resource got worse; The school calendar; A broken link | The school calendar | Holidays reduce visits for every component. | | 4 | Do these page views show that students learned? | Yes; No | No | A view is not a reader, and a reader is not a learner. | | 5 | What share of all views went to the simulation, to the nearest percent? | 25 percent; 33 percent; 45 percent | 25 percent | 860 divided by 3,500 is about 24.6 percent, which rounds to 25. | **Provenance:** The page views are illustrative examples made up for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative data". **Rules:** Month totals and the six-month totals are the sums of the values shown. Percentages are rounded to the nearest whole percent. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner hovers over bars to see exact values, and may toggle a component on or off. Toggling is not scored. 2. The learner presses Quiz and answers the five questions. 3. After question 5 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 5 questions in the order of the table, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [answer]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The answer is [answer]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 5 correct on the first attempt". At 4 or more it adds "You can read analytics with care." Below 4 it lists the Why text of each missed question. **Starting State:** The chart with all three components shown and the Quiz button. **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a page view is not a reader, a reader is not a learner, and holiday drops reflect the calendar.
